inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(0,48) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(0,48) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 48 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 48: a host write to 48 is overwritten on the next update. The retained script passes the key to S11.VBS, which writes 82; both right flippers move together.

inputs.label: Lower Left Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME left cabinet button bit 84 (CORE_SWLLFLIPBUTBIT). FLIP_SWNO(0,48) uses zero as the left sentinel: no left matrix copy exists and the ROM cannot read column 11 directly. With enable 23 on, this bit still synthesizes 47/48. Drive 84 for the left-flipper state; the table's extra matrix 47 write is to an unfitted position. The open cabinet contacts close while pressed, and both physical left flippers move together.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball closes 10; output 1 kicks it into the three-position trough. Output 8 feeds the next ball to shooter 11; the manual plunger launches it. The retained stack starts with three balls and uses 12, 13, 14 in feed-to-rear order. A ball holds its occupied contact; update occupancy as real balls roll, rather than toggling all sensors from the coil. Held/stuck contacts can provoke retries or switch diagnostics. Eject spring/cam and ball friction are table-owned tuning; C-8492 identifies the feed assembly.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball Trough, Outhole and Manual Shooter

mechanisms.behavior: D-9355 has three individually latching spring-retracted targets, one switch each and one common reset plunger/plate. A struck target drops and holds its contact until output 2 raises the bank and releases it. The table uses cvpmDropTarget 25-27. Game rules advance cave value, extra ball and special across completions. Reset retries, dirty contacts, binding guides and weak springs can cause stuck/dropped-target reports; no factory numeric reset duration is specified.
mechanisms.label: Three-Target Drop Bank

mechanisms.behavior: D-10883 contains four latching targets with four microswitches and two reset plungers/plates. Output 3 raises only the left pair 20/21, output 4 only right 22/23; the table uses separate two-target cvpmDropTarget instances. A hit starts the timed completion score sweep; physical targets stay down until reset. Do not model one common four-target reset. Sticking guides, switches or pair reset linkage can leave individual targets down.
mechanisms.label: Four-Target Flash Bank with Two Pair Resets

mechanisms.behavior: The A ramp feeds a serial three-ball lock sensed by 32, 33, 34, and output 5 drives the C-8492 eject cam at the release end. The retained script kicks from sw34. One/two locked balls plus top release target 24, or three locked balls, starts multiball and releases the lock; 2-ball scores 2X and 3-ball scores 3X. Sensors follow ball occupancy, not an electrical coil-to-switch relationship. Ball motion queues and jam/retry handling belong to the recreation; no exact ejection speed or delay is asserted.
mechanisms.label: Three-Ball Lock under A Ramp

mechanisms.behavior: Factory leaf scoring switches 43/44 are distinct from the special-solenoid trigger contacts. PinMAME deliberately uses 43/44 in ssSw to synthesize 17/18 while enable 23 is on. A ball flexes the sling rubber, closes the contact and the kicker accelerates it away; spring/linkage return releases the contact. The table animates each sling from its hit event. Rubber tension, leaf gaps and rebound are table tuning.
mechanisms.label: Left and Right Slingshot Kickers

mechanisms.behavior: Left cabinet button 45 requests magnetic rescue when a left charge is available. Output 9 energizes the 5580-09613-00 relay powering A-8447; the magnetic field acts on the ball near the left outlane. L-I-Z completion earns left units. The script uses cvpmMagnet LeftMagnet with grab-center disabled; its strength 12 is table tuning. The field stops when the ROM releases the relay or a charge expires. No position sensor or homing cycle exists.
mechanisms.label: Left Magna-Save

mechanisms.behavior: Right button 46 requests rescue and output 10 switches the right A-8447 through its relay. A-R-D completion earns right units. Right charge lamps 45-47 are depleted by separate presses, and output 19 flashes with the rescue. Ball response is force-based, not a held kicker. The script's magnet strength and event region are tuning, not factory measurements.
mechanisms.label: Right Magna-Save

mechanisms.behavior: Both right flippers follow the right cabinet button 82, both left follow 84. Outputs 45/46 and 47/48 are paired synthetic state, not four independent CPU coils or measured power/hold windings. Only the right lane-change contact is in the matrix at 48, copied from 82 by core_updateSw; there is no left matrix contact 47. Physical coils include lower FL23/600-30/2600 and upper FL24/600-30/2600, with return springs and separate physical EOS contacts. EOS contacts open at full stroke; the emulator models no EOS timing here.
mechanisms.label: Four Cabinet-Wired Flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Two passive ramp paths pass through the lizard head: left A 31 feeds the lock, right B 29 returns via the right route; 30 detects the right chute to the upper field and 42 the ramp tongue. Turnaround 15 scores the cave, and the top-right stationary target 24 serves the speed/release role. Spinner 28 pulses once per spin. The manual's numbered switch map and retained gates locate these contacts; ramp paths, passive gates and ball dwell require geometry rather than invented extra controller coils.
mechanisms.label: A/B Ramps, Cave, Turnaround and Ramp Tongue
